chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

A mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a sum for his freedom) dies having paid part of his manumission price, and he has a son by a concubine. He said: 'If it was stipulated that if he became unable [to pay], he would remain a slave, then his son returns as a slave, and the concubine [remains]. And if it was not stipulated, his son pays what remains of the manumission price, and inherits what remains.'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the price agreed upon for freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son and remaining debt of a slave who dies before completing his manumission contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal nuances of *mukatabah* (contractual manumission) upon the slave's death, emphasizing that the son's status depends on the specific contractual stipulation regarding residual debt. In the absence of such a clause, the son assumes the role of heir, paying the remaining balance to secure his own freedom and inheriting the estate, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of preserving liberty through financial obligation. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic inheritance law to balance the master's financial rights with the emancipation of the slave's lineage.
